items.q: How many revolutions did Russia have in 1917?
items.correct: Two — February (overthrew the Tsar) and October (Bolshevik takeover).
items.random_wrong: None — the Tsar gave up power voluntarily in peacetime.
items.why: The February Revolution ended Tsarism; the Bolsheviks seized power in October.

items.q: How did Stalin come to power?
items.correct: He won a power struggle through the 1920s, outmanoeuvring rivals like Trotsky.
items.misconception: He was Lenin's chosen successor and took over immediately.
items.random_wrong: He was elected by a national vote.
items.why: Stalin used his party position to defeat rivals after Lenin's death in 1924.

items.q: Did communism make everyone in the USSR equal and prosperous?
items.correct: No — there was repression, famine and a privileged party elite.
items.misconception: Yes, everyone became equal and wealthy.
items.random_wrong: The USSR had no government control of the economy.
items.why: Stalin's rule featured purges, the Gulag and famine (e.g. the Holodomor).
